MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
DevOps / Cloud Infrastructure | CI/CD & Test Infrastructure
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including hands-on ownership of CI/CD pipelines and test infrastructure for three product teams. Builds GitLab CI workflows and Helm-based ephemeral environments on a shared Kubernetes cluster, and has reduced pipeline runtime and test flakiness through practical automation and analysis. Personal infrastructure experience includes a k3s homelab with GitOps and monitoring, plus Terraform provisioning for a Hetzner VPS. Interested in moving into a DevOps or platform engineering role.

CORE SKILLS
Infrastructure & CI/CD: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes (namespace-level experience), Terraform (personal project), Argo CD
Systems & monitoring: Linux, PostgreSQL, Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, Traefik, cert-manager, TLS certificate management
Programming & automation: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL, Ansible (basic)
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Cloud learning: AWS EC2 and S3 basics (free-tier learning)

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (approximately 25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, and artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline runtime from 38 to 14 minutes by profiling workflows, parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end testing; monthly CI runner cost decreased by approximately 30%.
- Built short-lived, per-merge-request test environments with Docker Compose and later Helm on the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster. Environments include the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data, and are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky-test rate from 7% to under 1%.
- Developed Bash and Python tooling for PostgreSQL test-data seeding. Collected CI test results in PostgreSQL and created Grafana dashboards to help teams identify flaky tests.
- Wrote an internal guide to how the CI system works, now used in onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects through manual and automated testing.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node k3s cluster on Raspberry Pi 5 devices and deployed applications from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress, and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.

Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health | 2023–2024
- Delivered per-merge-request environments for the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data, deployed through GitLab CI and Helm to the shared Kubernetes cluster.
- Enabled QA and product colleagues to review features before merge and run end-to-end tests against the environments; configured automatic cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.

Flaky Test Dashboard | Odrava Health | 2023
- Stored CI test results in PostgreSQL and built Grafana dashboards showing flaky tests by team, supporting teams in identifying and fixing recurring issues.
- Contributed to a reduction in the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATION & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation; exam booked for January 2027 (not yet certified)

LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from QA automation into DevOps and test infrastructure. The professional summary is focused, and the experience section uses credible metrics: pipeline runtime reduced from 38 to 14 minutes, runner cost reduced by approximately 30%, and flaky tests reduced from 7% to under 1%. The selected projects reinforce the transition and demonstrate practical Kubernetes, GitOps, monitoring and Terraform exposure. The document is professional and appropriately transparent about namespace-level Kubernetes experience, personal Terraform work and CKA preparation. Its main content limitation is that it presents a compelling junior-to-mid DevOps profile, while the vacancy describes a contractor expected to shape production cloud architecture independently.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, reverse-chronological experience, plain text, and ATS-readable bullets. Relevant terms such as GitLab CI, Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, Docker, Linux, TLS, Prometheus, Grafana, PostgreSQL, Python and AWS are present. The format should parse reliably. AI screening probability is moderate to good for junior or mid-level DevOps/test-infrastructure roles, but lower for this specific vacancy because strong Terraform, Terragrunt, mTLS, networking, security, system design and production cloud operation are not evidenced. The skills section could be slightly improved by adding supported terms currently present only in the candidate material, especially Git, GitLab API and pytest-xdist.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the practical infrastructure, CI/CD, Linux, observability, analytical thinking and communication aspects of the role. It also provides credible evidence of ownership and stakeholder enablement through ownership of pipelines, the internal onboarding guide, mentoring, and environments used by QA and product colleagues. However, the candidate material indicates gaps against several central requirements: strong Terraform and Terragrunt, production cloud environment operation, system architecture/system design, mTLS, broader networking, practical security awareness, IoT or remote-device integration, and virtual machines. AWS exposure is limited to free-tier learning, and the Java experience is test automation rather than backend/full-stack development. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that can be fixed through wording. The role also appears to expect a more senior independent contractor profile than the CV currently establishes.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ATS enhancement: In the CORE SKILLS section, add the supported terms "Git", "GitLab API" and "pytest-xdist". For example, update the programming/automation line to include "Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL, GitLab API, pytest-xdist" and add Git to the Infrastructure & CI/CD line or a separate version-control entry.

MINOR alignment enhancement: In the PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY, make the boundary between professional and personal infrastructure experience even more explicit while foregrounding the strongest transferable evidence. For example, change the final two sentences to: "Professional experience includes GitLab CI ownership and Helm-based ephemeral environments on a shared Kubernetes cluster; personal infrastructure work includes a k3s homelab with GitOps and monitoring and Terraform provisioning for a Hetzner VPS. Interested in moving into a DevOps or platform engineering role." This preserves the existing truthful distinction while placing the most relevant infrastructure terms earlier.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable, and professionally presented. It gives strong quantified evidence for CI/CD ownership, pipeline optimisation, ephemeral environments, test reliability, and monitoring. The distinction between company experience, personal homelab work, and Terraform learning is generally clear and truthful. The strongest content is the 38-to-14-minute pipeline reduction, 30% runner-cost reduction, 900-test suite, and flaky-rate improvement from 7% to under 1%. The main content weakness is that the CV is stronger for QA/test infrastructure than for the target cloud infrastructure contractor role. It does not clearly frame the candidate's technical leadership, systems-design thinking, stakeholder coordination, practical security awareness, or networking knowledge beyond TLS certificate management. The selected projects section also repeats information already present under Odrava Health, which uses space without adding much new evidence.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses conventional section headings, standard reverse-chronological experience, searchable technology names, and ATS-friendly plain text formatting. It should parse reliably and has a good keyword base for GitLab CI, Kubernetes, Helm, Docker, Terraform, AWS, Linux, PostgreSQL, Prometheus, Grafana, TLS, and system monitoring. Its estimated AI/ATS screening probability is moderate rather than high for this specific vacancy: approximately 65-75%, depending on how heavily the screening system weights Terraform/Terragrunt, AWS, networking, security, and system-design evidence. The largest keyword and evidence weaknesses are Terragrunt, mTLS, network design, infrastructure security, cloud environment operation, systems architecture/system design, technical proposal leadership, and stakeholder alignment. Do not add unsupported keywords merely to improve matching. The existing qualification wording is appropriately cautious, especially for Kubernetes and Terraform.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV is a credible adjacent match for a junior-to-mid DevOps or platform-oriented role. It demonstrates hands-on CI/CD and test-environment infrastructure, namespace-level Kubernetes work, Helm deployments, observability, Linux, GitOps, and personal Terraform/AWS learning. This aligns with the ad's engineering-led, ownership-oriented environment and with supporting developers in making services observable and runnable. However, the role expects stronger production cloud infrastructure ownership than the candidate's material currently demonstrates. Terraform is personal rather than professional, Terragrunt is not present, AWS exposure is only basic learning, and there is no demonstrated IoT, train, automotive, remote-device, video-streaming, or telemetry-integration experience. The material also does not establish production on-call ownership, mTLS implementation, network design, or full system-architecture responsibility. These are candidate-profile gaps, not defects that rewriting can solve. The CV should nevertheless make the strongest truthful evidence more explicit: ownership of technical infrastructure topics, communication through documentation and mentoring, collaboration with QA/product stakeholders, analytical pipeline profiling, and secure TLS/observability practices.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE CHANGES
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the final sentence "Interested in moving into a DevOps or platform engineering role" with a role-aligned but truthful statement such as: "Transitioning from QA automation into DevOps and platform engineering, with hands-on experience owning CI/CD pipelines, Kubernetes-based test environments, infrastructure monitoring, and automation for three product teams." This makes the current match more concrete and uses the ad's infrastructure-engineering language without claiming production cloud ownership.

2. In the Odrava Health experience section, revise the first and third bullets to make technical ownership and environment operation clearer. For example, change the first bullet to: "Own and operate GitLab CI workflows for three product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end testing, artifact publishing, and CI troubleshooting." Change the ephemeral-environment bullet to: "Designed and implemented per-merge-request test environments using Docker Compose and Helm on the company's shared Kubernetes cluster; configured application, PostgreSQL and seeded-data deployment plus automatic cleanup." Do not describe this as cluster administration, because the original information specifies namespace-level access and platform-team ownership of the cluster.

3. In the Odrava Health experience section, add a bullet based on the candidate's original material that demonstrates communication and stakeholder enablement: "Wrote the internal guide to how the CI system works, now used for onboarding, and mentored two QA interns in 2023." Also incorporate the existing project evidence that QA and product colleagues reviewed features and ran end-to-end tests against the merge-request environments. This is the strongest truthful evidence for bringing stakeholders along and supporting other teams.

4. In the Core Skills section, make the security and networking wording more precise. Retain "TLS certificate management" and "cert-manager," but change the relevant line to something such as: "Networking & security: Traefik ingress, TLS certificate management, cert-manager, PostgreSQL connectivity, Linux networking basics." Only include "Linux networking basics" if the candidate can substantiate that knowledge; otherwise retain the existing Linux and TLS terms without implying broader networking expertise. Do not add mTLS, network design, or security engineering because they are not supported by the original information.

5. In the Core Skills section, change "Terraform (personal project)" to "Terraform (personal Hetzner VPS project)" and keep "Ansible (basic)" explicitly qualified. This preserves ATS visibility while clearly separating professional infrastructure work from personal infrastructure work. Do not add Terragrunt, since the candidate's original information does not mention it.

6. In the AWS line, change "AWS EC2 and S3 basics (free-tier learning)" to "AWS: EC2 and S3 basics through free-tier learning". This is more natural for ATS parsing and makes the level of exposure unambiguous. Do not imply AWS production experience.

MINOR / STRUCTURAL ENHANCEMENTS
7. Reduce duplication between the Odrava Health experience bullets and Selected Infrastructure Projects. Keep the detailed quantified results under Professional Experience, and use Selected Infrastructure Projects only for the homelab and the two projects that add distinct detail. Alternatively, remove the duplicate project descriptions and add a short "Selected Projects" subsection after Skills. This will make the CV more concise without losing evidence.

8. In the Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps entry, make the boundary between personal and professional experience even clearer by changing the heading to "Personal Infrastructure Project — k3s Homelab and Hetzner VPS". Retain the technologies and outcomes, but do not move it into employer work experience or present it as production cloud infrastructure.

9. In Certification & Professional Development, change "Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation; exam booked for January 2027 (not yet certified)" to "Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) — exam scheduled January 2027; not yet certified." This is shorter and less likely to be misread by an ATS or recruiter as an earned certification.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, credible CV for a QA-to-DevOps transition. It presents measurable outcomes, relevant infrastructure work, Kubernetes test-environment experience, monitoring, and personal cloud infrastructure clearly. The strongest evidence is the reduction of pipeline runtime from 38 to 14 minutes, the reduction in flaky tests from 7% to under 1%, and ownership of CI/CD workflows for three teams. The main content weakness is repetition in the Professional Summary: the first and final sentences both describe ownership of CI/CD pipelines and Kubernetes-based test environments. The CV also needs slightly clearer separation between professional experience, personal projects, and learning, particularly for Terraform, AWS, and the pending CKA exam.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses ATS-friendly section headings, standard reverse-chronological structure, plain text bullets, conventional job titles, and relevant keywords such as GitLab CI, Kubernetes, Helm, Docker, Terraform, Linux, PostgreSQL, Grafana, Prometheus, TLS, Python, and Bash. The quantified achievements should perform well in both keyword and AI screening. AI screening probability is reasonably strong for junior-to-mid DevOps, platform engineering, and CI/CD infrastructure roles, but weaker for this particular contractor role because the CV does not demonstrate Terragrunt, mTLS, broader AWS operation, production cloud infrastructure, or explicit systems architecture. Add the supported keyword Git, which appears in the original candidate information but is absent from the current CV. Also avoid placing an unearned certification too prominently: although the wording states that the CKA is not yet certified, some parsers may still interpret the heading as an achieved certification.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with hands-on infrastructure engineering through CI/CD ownership, Helm-based Kubernetes environments, Docker, monitoring, Terraform-based personal infrastructure, and Linux. It also demonstrates analytical thinking and communication through pipeline profiling, cost reduction, flaky-test analysis, dashboards, internal documentation, and mentoring. The candidate shows some relevant networking and security foundation through Traefik ingress, cert-manager, TLS, and certificate management. However, the candidate's material indicates gaps in strong Terraform and Terragrunt, mTLS, production AWS or other major-cloud operation, IoT or remote-device integration, backend/full-stack development, and virtual-machine experience. The CV is therefore a credible adjacent match rather than a direct match for a contractor expected to design fleet-connectivity infrastructure from the start and lead production cloud architecture. The ownership, collaboration, and engineering-led aspects of the role are supported, but stakeholder leadership could be made more explicit.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE CHANGES
1. In the Professional Summary, remove the repeated final sentence beginning "Transitioning from QA automation..." because it duplicates the preceding description of CI/CD ownership and Kubernetes test environments. Replace the summary with one concise paragraph that keeps the strongest evidence, for example: "QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including hands-on ownership of GitLab CI pipelines and Kubernetes-based test infrastructure for three product teams. Reduced pipeline runtime from 38 to 14 minutes and flaky-test rate from 7% to under 1%. Experienced with Helm, Docker, PostgreSQL, Linux, monitoring, Python and Bash automation, plus personal Terraform infrastructure on Hetzner and a k3s GitOps homelab. Transitioning into DevOps and platform engineering." Do not imply production-cluster ownership.
2. In the Core Skills section, add the supported keyword "Git" under "Infrastructure & CI/CD" or create a "Tools" grouping containing "Git, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes." This keyword is present in the original candidate information but currently omitted.
3. In the Certification & Professional Development section, split achieved certification from planned development. Change the current heading and entry to: "CERTIFICATIONS" followed by "ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019", then "PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT" followed by "Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam scheduled January 2027 — not yet certified." This prevents ATS or recruiter misinterpretation that CKA has already been obtained.
4. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, make the stakeholder and technical-leadership evidence more explicit without overstating authority. Add or revise a bullet to say: "Led the adoption of merge-request test environments across three product teams; documented the CI operating model for onboarding, and enabled QA and product colleagues to review features and run end-to-end tests before merge." This is supported by the original candidate information and better matches the requirement to lead technical topics and bring stakeholders along.
5. In the Homelab project entry, keep the label clearly as "Personal Project" or "Personal Infrastructure Project" and retain the words "personal" and "small Hetzner VPS." Do not present this work as commercial or production cloud infrastructure. The current placement under the overall experience area is acceptable only if its personal status remains unmistakable.

MINOR ATS / CLARITY ENHANCEMENTS
6. In the Core Skills section, change "Cloud learning: AWS: EC2 and S3 basics through free-tier learning" to "Cloud: AWS EC2 and S3 basics through free-tier learning; Hetzner VPS (personal Terraform project)." This keeps the AWS keyword while accurately signaling the limited level of experience.
7. In the Homelab entry, add the supported term "GitOps" to the first bullet or skills line if it is not already retained, for example: "Built a three-node k3s homelab with GitOps deployments through Argo CD." This is already supported by the candidate portfolio and is relevant to platform engineering.
8. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, retain the specific operational details "automatic cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity" and "shared Kubernetes cluster". These details make the ephemeral-environment work more concrete and demonstrate operational ownership without claiming cluster administration.
9. In the Skills section, retain the qualifier "namespace-level experience" beside Kubernetes and "personal" beside Terraform/Hetzner. These qualifiers are important truthfulness safeguards and should not be removed merely to increase keyword density.
